format: values are rows [start, end, size, count]: count values of size words, live over the closed interval [start, end]. budget = words 0..budget-1. align (default 1) applies to values wider than one word. semantics (default "abstract": values sharing a step conflict) may be "real": address_assign.rs intervals [def, last_read] with same-cycle reuse. Checked by verification/allocation_conjectures.py (A1-stored, A7-greedy-witnesses); see docs/ALLOCATION_CONJECTURES.md.

c1_counterexamples.name: pinning-k8-B16-unaligned
c1_counterexamples.demonstrates: Per-cycle load <= 16 at every step, yet no layout with vectors at any offset: two vectors fill steps 0 and 4, so the scalars of steps 1-3 are pinned into one 8-word half, and 9 are live at step 2.

c1_counterexamples.name: pinning-k8-B16-aligned
c1_counterexamples.demonstrates: Same with 8-aligned vector slots: the slots are the halves, so 3 steps and 2 vectors suffice.

c1_counterexamples.name: pinning-k8-B16-real
c1_counterexamples.demonstrates: The unaligned witness as real address_assign intervals [def, last_read] (abstract [s, e] -> [2s, 2e+1]); the closed per-cycle count is <= 16 at every cycle and no layout exists under the same-cycle-reuse rule.

c1_counterexamples.name: minimal-k2-B4-unaligned
c1_counterexamples.demonstrates: Smallest counterexample in time steps for sizes {1, 2} (found by the exhaustive search: none within 4 steps, this one at 5).

c1_counterexamples.name: sizes-2-3-B7
c1_counterexamples.demonstrates: Sizes that do not divide each other ({2, 3}) fail too, at B = 7 (exhaustive search: none at B = 6 within 6 steps).

greedy_failures.demonstrates: First fit puts the step-0 scalars at words 0 and 1; the vector at step 2 then has no 8 contiguous words, although putting the long scalar at word 8 works.
Lowest free 8-aligned slot: the scalar takes word 0 and blocks the only slot.
First fit with two vector-widths of room: the step-3 scalar reuses the dead vector's word 0 and splits the free space into 7 + 7 words.
Lowest free slot, aligned: the two scalars land in different slots, so no slot is free for the step-4 vector.
Most-recently-freed choice degenerates to first fit when nothing has been freed yet.
Reusing the most recently freed words (the dead vector's) fragments the space the step-4 vector needs.
Same, aligned: the second scalar goes to the slot vacated last instead of next to the first.
Scalars by lifetime from the top: the long scalar takes word 8, the only word the short one can use while the step-0 vector is live; swapping them works.
The vector goes to words 0-7 and the scalars fill 8-15 from the top, leaving the last short scalar no word; the vector at words 6-13 leaves room for all.
Vectors by lifetime: the step-2 vector takes slot 0 and the step-3 vector holds slot 1, so the scalar live over steps 2-3 has no word; the step-2 vector in slot 1 works.

C3's two-pass allocator outside its hypothesis (8 * 2 + 1 > 16): the step-5 vector takes the lowest slot without looking at scalars, so no word is free for the scalar over steps 2-7; slot 1 for it works.
